summary: HTTP/2 stream reuse header scope conflict triggers silent model fallback and mixed outputs for dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Vela Health (Dedicated) reports intermittent mixed-model responses and unexpected fallback to an older model variant during ongoing streaming sessions. The customer pins requests to redwood-open-13b-v2 but ~3-5% of streaming chunks are served by redwood-open-13b-v2-quant (older fallback) without an explicit routing event in control-plane logs.

Impact:
- Customers observe degraded output consistency in streamed completions (semantic differences and tokenization deltas).
- Billing anomaly: spikes in 'quant' model usage metrics leading to cost allocation confusion for dedicated capacity.
- Affects live endpoints handling health-care insurance claim summarization (high sensitivity).

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: cluster-id d-vela-west-1
- Region: us-west-2 (primary)
- Traffic pattern: HTTP/2 long-lived streaming connections (gRPC-web over H2), keepalive enabled.
- Pin config: route-level version_pin: redwood-open-13b-v2 (explicit).

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Open a long-lived streaming connection over H2 with multiplexing enabled (multiple concurrent streams per connection).
2) Send a pinned chat session that requests streaming tokens for ~30+ seconds.
3) Observe that some stream events contain tokenization differences and a change in latency profile mid-session.
4) Verify control-plane route mapping via /v1/routes/{route}/history — no explicit pin change recorded around observed time.

Observed behavior:
- ~3-5% of stream frames appear to be produced by the quantized variant (lower token width, slightly different detokenization).
- Edge logs show X-Redwood-Pin: redwood-open-13b-v2 on initial request, but downstream serving logs show a missing header on certain HTTP/2 stream IDs and a fallback decision in runtime.
- No orchestrator-promote/demote events in the same minute window.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming session pinned to configured model for entire session lifetime.
- Any fallback should be accompanied by a control-plane event and customer notification when pin is lost.

Relevant logs and traces (snippets):
- edge-proxy (us-west-2) trace id: trace-0ab3c7
  "stream_id=42 header_scope=connection X-Redwood-Pin=redwood-open-13b-v2"
- serving-runtime (gpu-02) log: "stream=42 missing pin-header; routing->fallback redwood-open-13b-v2-quant"
- billing metric: quant_model_tokens/hour rose +12% during incident window (03/10 16:12-16:18 UTC)

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Recommend switching to HTTP/1.1 streaming (no multiplex) for critical flows until fix is deployed.
- Force route config: add explicit per-stream metadata header X-Redwood-Force-Pin in client to reassert pin on each stream.

Investigation notes (internal):
- Hypothesis 1: HTTP/2 stream reuse with header scope=connection vs stream causes per-stream headers (X-Redwood-Pin) to be lost when the proxy reassigns stream IDs across backend connections during connection pooling.
- Hypothesis 2: Edge-proxy's header transform module normalizes pin header to connection-scoped metadata; when reused downstream the serving-runtime reads per-stream metadata and treats missing pin as eligible for fallback routing.
- Reproduced internally by running synthetic load with h2 multiplexing and toggling header scope (found reproducer at 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC).
- Reproducer shows ~4% of streams lose the per-stream header when the proxy merges multiplexed streams onto an existing backend connection.

Root-cause (preliminary):
- Edge-proxy optimization for backend connection reuse accidentally downgrades per-stream pin headers to connection scope in certain fast-path code paths, leading serving-runtime to interpret a missing per-stream pin as 'un-pinned' and invoke fallback routing.

Proposed fix:
1) Patch edge-proxy to preserve per-stream header delivery semantics for X-Redwood-Pin and X-Redwood-Force-Pin when multiplexing (hotfix branch edge-proxy/h2-pin-preserve).
2) Add defensive check in serving-runtime: treat absence of per-stream pin only if connection-level pin absent and control-plane indicates no explicit pin for that tenant.
3) Add observability: instrument edge-proxy to emit metrics: h2.streams_lost_pin_header, h2.streams_preserve_failures.

Next steps / rollout plan:
- 2026-03-12: Deploy edge-proxy hotfix to staging and run synthetic h2-multiplexing regression suite.
- 2026-03-13: Canary deploy to us-west-2 edge nodes with gradual traffic ramp (5% -> 25% -> 100%) monitoring h2.streams_lost_pin_header and quant model token % for Vela Health routes.
- 2026-03-14: If metrics stable, promote to all edge nodes in us-west-2 and communicate remediation to customer.

Audit / follow-up:
- Postmortem page scheduled: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INC/pages/H2+Pin+Leak+Postmortem (owner: Evan Brooks).
- Add automated regression to CI that simulates h2 multiplexing and asserts no per-stream header loss.
comments: 2026-03-10 17:05 - Riley Chen (Support): Initial triage from customer. Confirmed consistent reproduction with customer's HTTP/2 client. Escalated to SRE. SLA P1 acknowledged.

2026-03-10 19:22 - SRE (Evan Brooks): Reproducer built using h2load; confirmed per-stream header loss when proxy reuses backend connection. Captured packet-level trace showing header scope mismatch. Marked as potential regression in edge-proxy h2 fast-path.

2026-03-11 02:45 - Runtime Eng (Priya Kapoor): Added a defensive guard in serving-runtime to prefer connection-level pin if per-stream not present only when control-plane confirms no pin. Unit tests added. Preparing hotfix PR.

2026-03-11 11:10 - Support (Riley Chen): Communicated workaround to Vela Health — switch to HTTP/1.1 or include X-Redwood-Force-Pin per-stream. Customer accepted temporary workaround; they need timeline for a permanent fix.

2026-03-12 09:30 - SRE (Evan Brooks): Deployed edge-proxy/h2-pin-preserve to staging. Regression suite shows 0.1% failure compared to 4% baseline. Proceeding to canary tomorrow after additional monitoring hooks are added.
